design_principles: Every component must be combinable across genres, not locked to one mood
Each option is written as a directive prompt fragment that survives translation
Coverage spans editorial CG, documentary, surreal, retro, sport, food, tech, street, fashion, fantasy, horror-lite, sci-fi, slice-of-life
A viral Reel/Post needs: instant hook, readable emotion, rewatch reward, shareable detail, and rhythm — every dimension below targets at least one of these
Avoid template clichés: prompts force specificity (one focal point, one tonal direction, one motion intent) instead of generic adjectives

viral_factors.emotion_readability: must be nameable in one word within 2 seconds
viral_factors.rewatch_layer: one detail discoverable only on second viewing
viral_factors.shareability_cue: one element that triggers tag/save/quote behavior
viral_factors.rhythm_signature: motion + pacing must have a recognizable beat, not just movement

scene.prompt: Place the subject in an oversized workspace where scale contrast is the core idea — keyboard keys as platforms, paperclips as architecture, one human-scaled hero prop anchoring the eye.
Build a wide fantasy environment with three depth layers — foreground story prop, mid-ground subject action, distant mythic landmark — and one tiny character detail that rewards a second look.
Stage the scene in a lived-in domestic corner: tactile textiles, half-drunk mug, one personal artifact telling a backstory the viewer has to infer.
Compose a wet-asphalt night market scene with stacked neon signage, steam from a food cart catching backlight, and a single human silhouette that gives the chaos a center.
Build a liminal interior — fluorescent corridor, hotel pool at 3am, abandoned mall — with one impossible element placed casually so the viewer notices it on rewatch.
Set the scene on a rooftop edge with city horizon as the canvas — subject small against skyline, wind-implied hair or fabric, golden-hour or pre-storm sky doing emotional work.
Place the subject submerged with godrays piercing from above, suspended particles, fabric or hair drifting in slow drag — sound implied as muffled.
Use a clean studio seamless backdrop in a single saturated tone — subject dead-center or rule-of-thirds, one prop interaction, zero environmental clutter.
Frame a vast wilderness — alpine ridge, desert dune line, foggy forest — where the subject occupies less than 10% of the frame and the landscape becomes the protagonist.
Stage a maker's workshop with controlled chaos — tools mid-use, half-finished work, sawdust or paint residue — and one freshly completed object catching the cleanest light.
Capture a transit moment — empty train car, taxi back seat at night, escalator descent — where stillness inside contrasts motion outside the window.
Build a retro arcade interior — CRT glow on faces, sticky carpet patterns, cabinet attract-mode reflections — leaning into 80s/90s nostalgia without parody.
Frame a kitchen as a stage — flame flare, oil shimmer, knife rhythm on board — with the cook's hands doing the storytelling and ingredients staged like cast members.
Place the subject against industrial machinery scale — cargo crane, refinery pipework, mine truck — where rust, scale, and one human element create cinematic awe.
Discover a hidden garden pocket — overgrown greenhouse, mossy stone steps, wildflower tangle — lit as if found by accident, not staged.
Place a solo athlete in an empty stadium or training ground — pre-dawn, post-match, off-season — where echoing scale amplifies a private ritual.
Compose a clean tech lab — anti-static surfaces, blue task lighting, one device opened and exposed — with surgical visual hygiene and one warm human element to prevent coldness.
Capture marketplace density — produce stacks, fabric bolts, spice mounds — with one face making eye contact through the crowd as the emotional anchor.
Frame an abandoned grand interior — theater, ballroom, factory — where decay and original ornament fight for dominance and a single beam of light picks the focal point.
Catch an extreme weather instant — wall of rain, dust storm wall, blizzard whiteout, lightning flash — with the subject reacting honestly to the elements, not posing through them.

shot.prompt: Use a low-angle hero composition — camera below waist height, strong foreground anchor, clean silhouette against negative space.
Use a top-down overhead tableau where the full scene reads in one glance, with one dominant focal point breaking the symmetry.
Frame as a cinematic medium-wide — subject from knees up, environment doing 50% of the storytelling, lens around 35–50mm equivalent.
Use a deliberate dutch tilt — 8 to 15 degrees, motivated by emotion not gimmick — to create unease, energy, or off-balance narrative.
Shoot macro close-up where texture and material become the subject — pores, fabric weave, condensation, ink bleed — with razor-thin depth of field.
Use extreme wide framing where the subject is barely findable — environment dwarfs them, viewer has to search, payoff is the search itself.
Use over-the-shoulder POV that puts the viewer inside the action — partial subject occluding frame edge, attention forward, immersion through borrowed perspective.
Use rigid central symmetry — vanishing point dead center, mirrored elements, subject on the axis — for graphic calm and instant readability.
Use long-lens compression — 85 to 200mm equivalent — to flatten layers, isolate subject from background, and create that signature fashion/cinema look.
Use wide-angle distortion — 16 to 24mm equivalent, close to subject — for kinetic energy, exaggerated foreground, and that GoPro/skate-video punch.
Compose a two-shot where the gap, gaze, or gesture between two subjects carries the entire story — proxemics is the message.
Use frame-within-frame — doorway, window, mirror, screen — to focus attention and add a layer of voyeuristic distance.
Stage two focal planes that both demand attention — foreground object sharp, background subject equally sharp — creating compositional tension.
Push subject to one corner with 70%+ negative space — quiet, editorial, room for typography or breath.
Track laterally alongside the subject — parallel motion, parallax background — for that walking-with-a-friend energy or runway momentum.

lighting.prompt: Light with warm key against cool ambient fill — tungsten-vs-twilight, sodium-vs-moonlight — for emotional separation and instant cinematic read.
Use volumetric backlight with atmospheric haze — sun through dust, projector beam through fog — to carve depth and add scale.
Use soft north-window light with gentle falloff and tactile shadows — Vermeer logic, no harshness, every transition rendered patiently.
Light from a single visible practical — desk lamp, neon sign, phone screen, candle — and let everything else fall into honest shadow.
Use high-key lighting — bright, low-contrast, near-shadowless — for clean editorial, tech-product, or fashion-positivity feeling.
Use low-key chiaroscuro — 80% shadow, one decisive highlight on the subject — Caravaggio energy, drama through restraint.
Add neon rim lighting — magenta and cyan opposing rims — separating subject from background with music-video color logic.
Use low golden-hour sun — long warm rakes, long shadows, dust catching sidelight — natural and unforced, not orange-graded fake.
Shoot at blue hour — that 15-minute window of cobalt sky and warm interior windows — for urban melancholy without saying a word.
Embrace harsh midday sun — hard shadows as graphic shapes, blown highlights, surface heat implied — modern editorial defiance of golden-hour cliché.
Light from below the subject's eyeline — campfire, phone screen, computer glow — creating uncanny or sacred mood depending on color.
Use split lighting — one half of face lit, one half in shadow — to telegraph internal conflict, duality, or hidden truth.
Use dappled light through foliage, lace, blinds, or water — broken patterns dancing on surfaces — for memory-tinted, organic warmth.
Use studio strobe freeze — short flash duration, every droplet and fabric crease frozen — for sport, dance, or fashion impact.
Light the subject only with screen glow — phone, laptop, TV — flickering color shifts, modern digital-age intimacy or alienation.

style.prompt: Render with premium editorial polish — restrained texture detail, clean specular discipline, high-end commercial image hygiene, no AI-generic gloss.
Use painterly storybook texture — visible brush logic, simplified shape language, warm color harmony — Pixar-meets-Studio-Ghibli sensibility.
Aim for cinematic realism — believable materials, controlled contrast, intentional lens behavior, micro-imperfections on surfaces.
Adopt documentary unposed feel — caught-not-staged composition, real environmental sound implied, no makeup-perfect skin, dignified human truth.
Use modern anime 2D treatment — clean line art, cel-shading with one bounce, sky-blue and sunset-orange palette discipline, Makoto Shinkai light handling.
Emulate analog film — Portra-like skin, controlled grain structure, slight halation on highlights, color shifts in shadow regions.
Apply VHS lo-fi treatment — chroma bleed, scan lines, tracking errors as accent not noise — y2k or vaporwave context, used sparingly.
Use tilt-shift miniature effect — selective focus band, exaggerated saturation — making real scenes look like dioramas, real people like toys.
Render in isometric diorama — fixed 30/60 angle, stacked readable layers, every prop visible, game-and-infographic crossover.
Mimic claymation — fingerprint-textured surfaces, slight frame-to-frame jitter, handmade imperfection, Aardman/Laika DNA.
Adopt high-fashion editorial language — confident silhouettes, willful proportions, color blocking, Vogue-Italia-level commitment to attitude.
Channel raw street photography — decisive-moment timing, available light only, slight motion blur tolerated, Daido Moriyama or Alex Webb DNA.
Treat the frame as a graphic poster — bold typography space, two-color discipline, Swiss-design grid logic, no decoration without function.
Use high-contrast B&W noir — crushed shadows, hot specular highlights, smoke or rain implied — 1940s detective DNA without costume cliché.
Render in infrared-style palette — pink/white foliage, deep cyan skies, alien-pastoral feeling — used purposefully as dream signal.
Apply comic halftone treatment — Ben-Day dots, ink-line emphasis, limited primary palette — Lichtenstein-meets-Saul-Bass attitude.
Use Y2K chrome glossy aesthetic — liquid metal text, blue-tinted lens flares, optimistic-future-from-the-past vibe, Matrix-meets-iPod era.
Render low-poly with warmth — faceted geometry but soft ambient shading, indie-game-poster sensibility, Monument-Valley-adjacent calm.

color.prompt: Restrict palette to two dominant hues plus neutrals — every accent earns its place, every saturation choice deliberate, ad-poster discipline.
Use a near-monochrome scene plus one saturated accent — a red coat in grayscale street, a yellow taxi in blue dusk — guaranteed eye anchor.
Use muted earth tones — clay, oat, sage, stone — desaturated but not lifeless, premium-natural-brand palette discipline.
Crank candy saturation — bubblegum pink, lemon yellow, mint, lavender — Z-gen confectionery palette, joyful and unapologetic.
Anchor in ember tones — amber, ochre, terracotta, soot — fire-lit logic, comfort and slight danger coexisting.
Use a sub-zero palette — ice blue, gunmetal, frost white, deep navy — clinical or wintry depending on context, never warm.
Use synthwave gradient — magenta to indigo to cyan — sky-as-canvas treatment, retro-future emotional shorthand.
Pretend the image has been sun-bleached — pastels with reduced contrast, slight cyan shift in shadows — Polaroid-from-the-attic memory color.
Use Bauhaus primaries — red, yellow, blue, plus black and white — high-contrast, zero apology, design-history-aware.
Stay within one hue family — varied value and saturation, no contrasting hue — for serene tonal harmony, interior-magazine calm.
Use teal-orange blockbuster grade — skin warmed, shadows pushed teal — used knowingly as cinema reference, not by accident.
Place saturated neon accents against concrete-gray environment — color earns weight by scarcity, city-night logic.

subject_archetype.prompt: Cast a quiet observer archetype — present but not performing, reading the room, the kind of character whose stillness implies depth.
Cast a craftsperson at work — confident hands, worn tools, quiet expertise communicated through small efficient motions, not exposition.
Cast an underdog mid-effort — sweat, breath, a body fighting through resistance — relatable struggle, no hero polish.
Cast an elder treated with dignity — weathered hands or face foregrounded, life implied in posture, never reduced to nostalgia prop.
Cast a child mid-wonder — concentration on something adults dismiss, scale exaggerated by their smallness, never cute-cliché.
Cast an outsider mid-context — overdressed at the bus stop, calm in the chaos, the wrong-looking person who's actually the right one.
Cast a duo with silent understanding — old friends, working partners, parent-and-child — communicating through shared rhythm, not dialogue.
Cast an anthropomorphic creature — tiny clothes, human posture, animal logic — charm through specificity of behavior, not generic cuteness.
Treat an object as the protagonist — a single shoe, a kettle, a lamp — given screen presence usually reserved for human leads.
Treat the crowd as a single character — synchronized motion, collective breath, one face surfacing then disappearing back into the body.
Stage a confrontation between two versions of the same person — mirror, doppelganger, before-and-after — internal conflict externalized.

emotion.prompt: Aim for bittersweet loneliness with quiet dignity — not empty sadness, not self-pity, the kind that includes acceptance.
Aim for warm healing — softness, safety, the feeling of being held — instantly nameable in one second.
Lean into playful absurdity — contrast and timing as the joke, not chaos, the smile-and-rewind kind of humor.
Build tense anticipation — something is about to happen but hasn't yet, every detail loaded, viewer breath held.
Capture triumphant release — the exhale after effort, arms unclenching, the moment after winning, not the act itself.
Render sharp focus emotion — total absorption in task, world narrowed to one target, no awareness of camera or audience.
Create uncanny unease — almost-right but slightly wrong, no jump scare, the kind that makes viewers pause and squint.
Show tender devotion — care expressed through small gestures, attention to another's needs, love without performance.
Express yearning — gaze toward something just out of reach, body forward, want made visible through posture not face.
Show quiet pride — small smile, straight shoulders, the look of someone who knows what they did and isn't going to brag.
Render contained anger — jaw set, breath measured, fury held under tension — far more powerful than expression.
Catch unguarded delight — pre-laugh moment, eyes lighting before mouth moves, the joy you can't fake.
Show exhausted acceptance — the seat-edge sit, the long exhale, the it-is-what-it-is look that adults recognize immediately.
Capture first-sight wonder — the half-second before words, mouth slightly parted, body still — encountering the impossible as plausible.
Express reckless freedom — body abandoned to motion, no fear of consequence, the kind of moment people post and caption with one word.

hook.prompt: Make the first read about scale contrast — tiny vs huge, wide vs narrow — instant curiosity in under a second.
Set up an unexpected role — wrong character in right uniform, or right character in wrong context — readable in one second.
Use a quiet emotional reveal — subtle, sticky, one detail that rewards a second look and a third share.
Break an expected visual pattern — symmetry interrupted, repetition with one wrong unit — disruption forces attention.
Lead with a first frame that makes the viewer say 'wait, what' — impossible juxtaposition, mid-action freeze, scroll-stop bait.
Frame the opening as a promise — something is being prepared, hidden, or about to be revealed — viewer stays for the answer.
Mirror an exact relatable moment — the 3pm slump, the elevator silence, the parking-lot post-shop sit — instant 'this is me' recognition.
Imply transformation without showing it linearly — one frame containing both states, viewer's brain fills the gap.
Set up a tasteful debate trigger — pineapple-on-pizza-level disagreement — comment-section gold without actual harm.
Open with the promise of satisfying completion — neat slice, perfect fit, clean reveal — process-porn instinct.
Show an unfamiliar object or unidentifiable action — viewer must keep watching to learn what it is, dwell-time engineered.
Plant a niche cultural reference visible only to the in-group — local dialect prop, subculture detail — tribe-recognition trigger.

motion.prompt: Use a slow push-in — gradual zoom or dolly toward emotional center, scene logic stays fixed, intensity rises.
Use a parallax fly-through — camera moves through layered depth, subject locked as anchor, foreground elements pass like punctuation.
Reveal the scene quickly, then hold long enough for the emotional payoff to land — silence after the punchline.
Use match-cut between two scenes that share shape or motion — bone to spaceship logic — sells transformation through visual rhyme.
Use a whip pan to slingshot between moments — motion-blurred transition, kinetic energy carried into next beat.
Lock the camera completely still — let only subjects move — tableau-vivant logic, every motion inside frame becomes meaningful.
Use speed ramps — normal to slow at the impact moment, fast through transitions — engineered viewer-breath rhythm.
Orbit smoothly around the subject — 90 to 360 degrees — every angle adding information, common in product but underused in narrative.
Move camera vertically — drone rise revealing scale, top-down descent into intimacy — vertical motion as emotional escalator.
Use stop-motion-style jitter — slight inter-frame inconsistency — handcraft signal, indie warmth, anti-AI-perfection statement.
Engineer a seamless loop — end frame matches start frame, viewer can't tell where it began — engineered rewatchability.
Use sudden freeze-frame at peak moment — motion locks, text or sound enters, emphasis weaponized.
Use honest handheld — micro-shake, breath rhythm visible, viewer feels embodied — documentary or first-person POV signal.
Cut to beat — every action lands on a music hit, rhythm is the structure — trend-aware short-form DNA.

sound_design_cue.prompt: Imply ASMR sound logic — close-mic textures, paper crinkle, ice clink, fabric slide — sound becomes the reason to wear headphones.
Imply quiet room tone — fridge hum, distant street, no music — silence as the loudest design choice.
Imply a rising synth swell — pad pushing toward crescendo, sub-bass entering — emotional escalator, sci-fi or sport hype.
Imply a lo-fi warm loop — crackle, brushed snare, mellow piano — study-with-me, late-night-calm signal.
Imply one decisive diegetic sound — door slam, knife hit, glass clink — emphasized by silence around it, more cinematic than score.
Imply sudden silence — music or noise stops mid-phrase — viewer's body tenses, attention sharpens involuntarily.
Imply close-mic voiceover — breath audible, conversational not performative — letting-you-in-on-a-secret intimacy.
Compose with awareness of a trending audio rhythm — beats and visual cuts pre-aligned for that audio's structure — algorithm-aware.
Imply layered field recording — birds, distant traffic, footsteps on specific surface — texture stacked for honest sense of place.

text_overlay_strategy.prompt: Use zero text overlay — visual carries 100% of the meaning — confidence move, premium signal.
Drop one perfectly weighted line of text — quotable, screenshot-worthy, placed where eye lands second.
Use kinetic typography on beat — words snap in with motion, scale-and-position varies, treated as character not subtitle.
Use handwritten-style text overlay — diary feeling, personal voice, trembling slightly imperfect — anti-corporate intimacy.
Use clean data labels — arrows pointing to elements, numeric callouts — infographic logic, useful for explainer or tutorial.
Sync caption to lyric — each line appears on the beat it's sung, karaoke-but-cinematic — trend-aware emotional shorthand.
Use one iconic word in poster-grade typography — one word doing all the work, magazine-cover discipline.

rewatch_layer.prompt: Plant one easter egg in the background — tiny visual joke, hidden character, signage callback — found only on second viewing.
Write a caption with two readings — first pass funny, second pass emotional, or vice versa — comment-section gold.
Hide a recurring motif — same color, same shape, same number appearing three times — viewer notices only on rewatch.
Insert a micro-expression — a flicker of doubt, glance, smile-correction — half a second long, changes the whole meaning.
Plant a foreshadow that pays off later in the same shot — object that becomes important, sound that returns — tight narrative satisfaction.
Use an unusual perspective that takes a beat to parse — viewer 'gets it' on second look — perspective puzzle as engagement.

narrative_structure.prompt: Drop the viewer in mid-action — no setup, context inferred while watching — instant scroll-stop, exposition forbidden.
Set up a clean expectation in first beats, deliver a clean payoff in last beats — Aesop discipline at TikTok speed.
Build toward an obvious outcome, then deliver the opposite — controlled subversion, the twist must feel earned not random.
Structure the piece as a loop — last frame leads back to first frame — engineered for replay and ambient watching.
Use a list structure — three or five beats, numbered visually or rhythmically — content-creator backbone for skimmable depth.
Tell a transformation in three beats — before, during, after — process-content backbone, satisfaction guaranteed.
Hold one unbroken moment — no cuts, no time jumps — real-time discipline, the brave format.
Open with a question that demands an answer — visually or in text — viewer commits because their brain wants resolution.
Build energy toward something big, then deliberately undercut it — the joke or art statement is the deflation itself.
